title: Maximum Profitable Triplets With Increasing Prices I
summary: Given arrays prices and profits of length n, find the maximum profit from picking three items where the item prices strictly increase and the total profit is the sum of their individual profits.
statement: Given arrays prices and profits of length n, find the maximum profit from picking three items where the item prices strictly increase and the total profit is the sum of their individual profits. Return -1 if no such triplet exists.
constraints: Choose indices i<j<k with strictly increasing prices.
Return the maximum sum of their profits, or -1 when no such triplet exists.
hints: Fixing the middle separates the choices into independent left and right maxima.
For each middle, find the best earlier lower-price profit and later higher-price profit.
Combine both maxima with the middle profit when each exists.
Every legal triplet has one middle and its best outer choices are independent once that middle is fixed.
editorial: Every legal triplet has one middle and its best outer choices are independent once that middle is fixed.

tests.explanation: Prices two,three,four at indices one,two,three yield profit 2+7+10=19.
The last three increasing prices maximize the profit sum at twelve.
